records: A consumer can apply to an ADR scheme if a provider has not resolved a complaint within eight weeks, or if deadlock is reached earlier.
Ofcom received more than 58,316 consumer contacts by calls, web forms, emails and letters in 2023/24.
Ofcom does not resolve individual telecoms complaints.
Complaint data informs Ofcom policy, enforcement and monitoring work.
Ofcom has published quarterly residential complaints data by provider since April 2011.
The methodology states that no single information source gives a complete picture of provider performance.
One publication objective is transparency of data.
One publication objective is helping citizens and consumers use a competitive market.
One publication objective is incentivising improved provider performance.
The publication focuses on residential landline, fixed broadband, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV complaints.
A single contact can contain complaints about more than one separate matter.
Ofcom generally records the two most serious matters per service when more than two are raised.
Complainants raising more than two matters for one service account for about 1% or less of complainants for each service.
An average of 1.5 complaints was recorded per consumer contact in 2021.
Fixed broadband in the methodology includes ADSL, cable and fibre services.
Pay-monthly mobile includes data used through a mobile handset.
Landline includes providers supplying line rental and calls as well as calls-only services.
Pay-TV complaints cover access to the service, not complaints about programme content.
Fixed Wireless Access is not generally included in the fixed-broadband definition.
Where a provider offers FWA alongside fixed broadband and complaints cannot be separated, both FWA complaints and subscribers are included.
The published data covers complaints reported to Ofcom and is only a partial picture of complaints about a provider.
Ofcom does not check the veracity of each individual complaint.
Contact volumes may reflect the quality of a provider's complaints handling as well as service quality.
Enforcement publicity, network failures or service changes can cause spikes in Ofcom contact volumes.
Smaller operators are more likely to show larger short-term fluctuations because their subscriber bases are smaller.
For an unknown-provider transfer, a verified transfer request is recorded against the provider that made the request.
If no transfer request is found, the complaint is recorded against the existing provider.
The report generally includes providers with a stable market share of 1.5% or more in the relevant market.
A provider is generally removed after its market share remains below 1.5% for four consecutive quarters.
Reports for periods before Q2 2014 retained the earlier general inclusion criteria of 4% market share and at least 30 complaints per month.
The providers in scope account for at least 91% of every market covered.
The provider scope represents at least 91% of the landline market.
